summary: Select compatible eager/full/partial replay by measured costs and retain reproducible per-shape implementation choices
implementation_scope: Python and header-only C++20 recorded choice tables and repeatability checks, plus a portable Python phase/shape/capability/memory replay selector with cold-setup amortization, and a cuBLASLt binding that pins one recorded split-K-free algorithm per prompt GEMM shape; candidate execution, native capture and costs are engine supplied

agent_guidance.use_when: The engine chooses among interchangeable implementations whose rounding differs, or among supported eager/full/partial execution offers with measured costs and memory limits
agent_guidance.avoid_when: Only one execution path is available and reproducible, or replay offers lack trustworthy compatibility identities and costs
provides: Power-of-two width buckets with a minimum and cap, and canonical shape keys
Choice table: recorded indices replay exactly, tuning picks the fastest with lower-index ties and skips candidates that cannot run, otherwise candidate 0
Export of every choice as a flat JSON table for the frozen configuration, and a strict native parser
Out-of-range detection when a recorded index exceeds the current candidate list
Cross-process repeatability runner with first differing JSON path and sequence index, usable as functional-check evidence
Compatible eager/full/partial selection using measured run/setup costs, memory limits and explicit padding permission

Pinned prompt GEMMs in every cuBLASLt prompt format (FP16, BF16 and FP32; FP8 e4m3/e5m2 and mixed pairs, unscaled, per-tensor or per-row scaled; block-scaled MXFP8, MXFP4 and NVFP4; to BF16, FP16 or FP32): one recorded split-K-free cuBLASLt algorithm per shape and format for every row count, recorded row-exact and fastest per row, with faster bit-identical algorithms for short row buckets, refused on another device or cuBLASLt version
engine_supplies: Stable candidate lists per key (for example a library heuristic list queried at the bucket width)
Synchronized device timing on representative inputs and a warm-up pass per bucket
Exact-shape acceptance check before reusing a bucket choice at another width, with a deterministic fallback
Library version and device identity stored beside the table, and the command that writes comparable output
Complete backend/representation/allocation identities, supported execution offers and revalidated launch resources
preserve: Timing never runs on the serving path; recorded choices replay exactly
Candidate order is reproducible for the recorded software and device
A bucket choice is used at another width only when the backend accepts it
Repeatability compares complete outputs of separate processes
adapt: Key dimensions, bucket minimum and cap
Warm-up widths and the compared output format

code_files.purpose: Width buckets, keys, table validation and the recorded/tuned/fallback choice table with export
Header-only C++20 buckets, choice table with timing callback, JSON export and strict parser
Runs a command in fresh processes and reports the first differing JSON path and sequence index
Backend-neutral eager/full/partial replay choice with complete identities, padding permission, memory feasibility and amortized measured costs
Records, tables and replays one row-exact split-K-free cuBLASLt algorithm per prompt GEMM shape

cuBLASLt binding: split-K-free heuristic candidates, one plan per recorded algorithm, per-row-count checks and GEMMs in every format: 16-bit, FP32, FP8 with tensor or row scales, block-scaled MXFP8, MXFP4 and NVFP4

requires.hardware: Python 3.11+ standard library; C++20 standard library for the native table; pinned_gemm needs PyTorch, a C++ compiler and cuBLASLt on a CUDA GPU; its FP8 formats need compute capability 8.9 or later and MXFP8, MXFP4 and NVFP4 10.0 or later, as cuBLASLt offers them
requires.model: No model or tensor layout requirement
requires.workload: Any engine that selects among implementations per shape, and any command that can write its result as JSON

contract.input: Operation names, shape dimensions and widths; candidate counts with an optional timing callback; a recorded flat JSON table; a command containing {output}
contract.output: (index, source) per key, an exported table, and a repeatability report with per-run digests and first differences
contract.ownership: The table owns its recorded and chosen maps; the engine owns candidates, plans and timing; the runner owns its temporary output directory
contract.failure: Reject non-positive widths, non-power-of-two minimums, widths above the cap, empty candidate lists, recorded indices beyond the list, malformed tables and commands without {output}; a failed run reports exit status 2
contract.core_boundary: No Core change; choices live in the engine configuration and the runner is a check tool outside the serving path

dependencies: C++20 standard library for the native table
PyTorch with torch.utils.cpp_extension and cuBLASLt for pinned_gemm

validation.host: Buckets and caps, keys, table validation, tuning ties and unavailable candidates, replay without timing, out-of-range indices, difference reports for values, lengths, types and nested sequences, and fresh-process runs that are identical, different or failing; Replay amortization, phase/identity gates, padding, resident/cold memory limits and partial fallback; pinned GEMM table keys, format parsing, blocked scale layout and padding, file round trip with and without short buckets and device/version refusal
validation.native: Header-only table: bucket rules, tuning ties, replay without timing, fallback, out-of-range indices, to_json/parse round trip and malformed tables; pinned GEMMs on CUDA: for every format the GPU takes, rows bit-identical across prompt lengths and close to torch or the FP32 dequantized product; formats the GPU lacks skipped with the reason
validation.performance: No speed or determinism claim for any candidate; both are the engine's measurements
